speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me if you have experienced any recent head trauma, neck stiffness, or sensitivity to light? Also, have you noticed any rashes or difficulty moving any part of your body?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of tics and current haloperidol use, I need to rule out neuroleptic malignant syndrome; do you have any muscle rigidity or excessive sweating? I will also check for a rash to exclude meningitis, so please remain still while I examine your neck and skin.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of fever, altered mentation, generalized rigidity, and profuse sweating in a patient taking haloperidol is highly suggestive of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. To confirm this diagnosis, I need to check for elevated creatine kinase levels and signs of autonomic instability.
